input.content:
# SOP-ASM-001 — Handling assessment and amendment enquiries
#
# Class: assessment_and_amendment (auto_answerable).
#
# TIE-BREAK RULE (see sop_design.md S10.3): ASM-001 and FIL-001 both touch
# objecting to a Notice of Assessment. Any enquiry that DISPUTES THE FIGURES in
# an assessment — including an estimated NOA raised for late filing — is
# `assessment_and_amendment`, not `filing`. `filing` covers only how and when to
# submit a return. This rule is binding on the email generator so that the
# overlap does not produce mislabelled ground truth.

sop_id: SOP-ASM-001
title: Handling assessment and amendment enquiries
version: "1.0"
effective_date: 2026-01-01
supersedes: null
applies_to_ya: [2025, 2026]
intents: [assessment_and_amendment]
indexed: true
owner_queue: IIT-General          # INVENTED — not a real IRAS queue
handling_target: 5_working_days   # ILLUSTRATIVE — not a real IRAS SLA
auto_reply_permitted: true
escalate_if:
  - account_specific
  - amount_computation_requested
  - hardship_or_waiver_request

references:
  - id: understanding_assessment
    url: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/receive-tax-bill-pay-tax-check-refunds/understanding-my-tax-assessment
    fetched: 2026-09-01
  - id: amend_bill
    url: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/receive-tax-bill-pay-tax-check-refunds/making-changes-after-filing-receiving-tax-bill
    fetched: 2026-09-01
  - id: tax_bill
    url: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/receive-tax-bill-pay-tax-check-refunds/getting-my-tax-assessment
    fetched: 2026-09-01

scope: >
  Taxpayer asks what a Notice of Assessment means, what the different NOA types
  are, how to read the terms on a tax bill, how to amend an assessment, how to
  object to one, or what happens while an objection is under review.

not_in_scope:
  - text: The figures in this taxpayer's own assessment, or the status of their own objection.
    route_to: account_specific
  - text: How or when to submit a return, and filing deadlines.
    route_to: filing                        # TIE-BREAK: mechanics of filing belong to FIL-001
  - text: Recomputing tax, reliefs or a revised balance for the taxpayer.
    route_to: amount_computation_requested
  - text: Asking for a penalty arising from the assessment to be waived.
    route_to: hardship_or_waiver_request

facts:
  - text: >
      A Notice of Assessment (Original) is the tax bill computed from the tax
      form(s) submitted and information sent by organisations participating in
      the Auto-Inclusion Scheme.
    source: understanding_assessment
  - text: >
      A Notice of Assessment (Amended) is issued when an assessment is amended
      downwards, resulting in a reduction in tax payable — for example on the
      inclusion of reliefs or a reduction in income.
    source: understanding_assessment
  - text: >
      A Notice of Assessment (Additional) is issued when an assessment is amended
      upwards, resulting in additional tax payable — for example on the
      withdrawal of reliefs or the inclusion of additional income.
    source: understanding_assessment
  - text: >
      A Notice of Assessment (Estimated) may be issued where a return has not been
      filed by the due date, estimating tax from available information. The
      taxpayer must still file the return for IRAS to issue an amended or
      additional assessment.
    source: understanding_assessment
  - text: >
      Year of Assessment (YA) is the tax year in which income tax is calculated
      and charged, on income earned in the preceding calendar year. Income taxed
      in YA 2026 is income earned from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025.
    source: understanding_assessment
  - text: >
      A return filed online may be re-filed once, by 18 April. Otherwise the tax
      bill is amended through the 'Amend Tax Bill' digital service at myTax
      Portal.
    source: amend_bill
  - text: >
      Amendments must be filed within 30 days from the date stated on the income
      tax bill (the Notice of Assessment). IRAS reviews the amendment and informs
      the taxpayer of the outcome.
    source: amend_bill
  - text: >
      The 'Amend Tax Bill' digital service may be used to revise an income
      declaration, to add or amend claims for deductions and reliefs, and to claim
      Parenthood Tax Rebate.
    source: amend_bill
  - text: >
      The obligation to pay is not suspended by an objection: tax must be paid
      within 1 month of the Notice of Assessment, and a late payment penalty
      applies to tax outstanding after 1 month, even where an objection is under
      review.
    source: amend_bill
  - text: >
      Where an assessment is revised after an objection is reviewed, any credit
      balance is refunded within 30 days from the date of the new tax bill, the
      Notice of Assessment (Amended).
    source: amend_bill
  - text: >
      The re-filing route by 18 April does not apply to taxpayers under the Direct
      Notice of Assessment (D-NOA) scheme.
    source: amend_bill

decision_steps:
  - condition: Asking about the figures in their own assessment, or the status of their own objection
    action: Escalate
    reason: account_specific
  - condition: Asking IRAS to recompute their tax, relief or revised balance
    action: Escalate
    reason: amount_computation_requested
  - condition: Asking for a penalty to be waived because of the assessment
    action: Escalate
    reason: hardship_or_waiver_request
  - condition: Asking only how or when to file a return, with no dispute about figures
    action: Route to SOP-FIL-001
    reason: tie_break_filing_mechanics
  - condition: Otherwise
    action: Explain the assessment type and the amendment route from the key facts

approved_phrasing:
  - id: noa_types
    text: >
      A Notice of Assessment (Original) is the tax bill computed from the return
      you filed together with information provided under the Auto-Inclusion
      Scheme. A Notice of Assessment (Amended) is issued when your assessment is
      revised downwards, and a Notice of Assessment (Additional) when it is
      revised upwards. A Notice of Assessment (Estimated) may be issued where a
      return has not been filed by the due date; you must still file the return so
      that the assessment can be revised.
  - id: amend_window
    text: >
      If you need to make a change after receiving your tax bill, you may file an
      amendment using the 'Amend Tax Bill' digital service at myTax Portal within
      30 days from the date on your Notice of Assessment. IRAS will review the
      amendment and inform you of the outcome.
  - id: pay_while_objecting
    text: >
      Please note that filing an objection does not defer payment. Tax is due
      within 1 month of the date of your Notice of Assessment, and a late payment
      penalty applies to tax outstanding after that date even while an objection
      is being reviewed. If your assessment is revised, any credit balance is
      refunded within 30 days from the date of the amended tax bill.
  - id: ya_meaning
    text: >
      The Year of Assessment is the year in which tax is calculated and charged on
      income earned in the preceding calendar year. For example, Year of
      Assessment 2026 covers income earned from 1 January to 31 December 2025.

do_not:
  - Do not comment on the figures in a specific taxpayer's assessment.
  - Do not predict the outcome of an objection or amendment.
  - Do not recompute tax, reliefs or a revised balance.
  - Do not advise that payment may be withheld pending an objection.

related:

# SOP-ASM-001 — Handling assessment and amendment enquiries
#
# Class: assessment_and_amendment (auto_answerable).
#
# TIE-BREAK RULE (see sop_design.md S10.3): ASM-001 and FIL-001 both touch
# objecting to a Notice of Assessment. Any enquiry that DISPUTES THE FIGURES in
# an assessment — including an estimated NOA raised for late filing — is
# `assessment_and_amendment`, not `filing`. `filing` covers only how and when to
# submit a return. This rule is binding on the email generator so that the
# overlap does not produce mislabelled ground truth.

sop_id: SOP-ASM-001
title: Handling assessment and amendment enquiries
version: "1.0"
effective_date: 2026-01-01
supersedes: null
applies_to_ya: [2025, 2026]
intents: [assessment_and_amendment]
indexed: true
owner_queue: IIT-General          # INVENTED — not a real IRAS queue
handling_target: 5_working_days   # ILLUSTRATIVE — not a real IRAS SLA
auto_reply_permitted: true
escalate_if:
  - account_specific
  - amount_computation_requested
  - hardship_or_waiver_request

references:
  - id: understanding_assessment
    url: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/receive-tax-bill-pay-tax-check-refunds/understanding-my-tax-assessment
    fetched: 2026-09-01
  - id: amend_bill
    url: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/receive-tax-bill-pay-tax-check-refunds/making-changes-after-filing-receiving-tax-bill
    fetched: 2026-09-01
  - id: tax_bill
    url: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/receive-tax-bill-pay-tax-check-refunds/getting-my-tax-assessment
    fetched: 2026-09-01

scope: >
  Taxpayer asks what a Notice of Assessment means, what the different NOA types
  are, how to read the terms on a tax bill, how to amend an assessment, how to
  object to one, or what happens while an objection is under review.

not_in_scope:
  - text: The figures in this taxpayer's own assessment, or the status of their own objection.
    route_to: account_specific
  - text: How or when to submit a return, and filing deadlines.
    route_to: filing                        # TIE-BREAK: mechanics of filing belong to FIL-001
  - text: Recomputing tax, reliefs or a revised balance for the taxpayer.
    route_to: amount_computation_requested
  - text: Asking for a penalty arising from the assessment to be waived.
    route_to: hardship_or_waiver_request

facts:
  - text: >
      A Notice of Assessment (Original) is the tax bill computed from the tax
      form(s) submitted and information sent by organisations participating in
      the Auto-Inclusion Scheme.
    source: understanding_assessment
  - text: >
      A Notice of Assessment (Amended) is issued when an assessment is amended
      downwards, resulting in a reduction in tax payable — for example on the
      inclusion of reliefs or a reduction in income.
    source: understanding_assessment
  - text: >
      A Notice of Assessment (Additional) is issued when an assessment is amended
      upwards, resulting in additional tax payable — for example on the
      withdrawal of reliefs or the inclusion of additional income.
    source: understanding_assessment
  - text: >
      A Notice of Assessment (Estimated) may be issued where a return has not been
      filed by the due date, estimating tax from available information. The
      taxpayer must still file the return for IRAS to issue an amended or
      additional assessment.
    source: understanding_assessment
  - text: >
      Year of Assessment (YA) is the tax year in which income tax is calculated
      and charged, on income earned in the preceding calendar year. Income taxed
      in YA 2026 is income earned from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025.
    source: understanding_assessment
  - text: >
      A return filed online may be re-filed once, by 18 April. Otherwise the tax
      bill is amended through the 'Amend Tax Bill' digital service at myTax
      Portal.
    source: amend_bill
  - text: >
      Amendments must be filed within 30 days from the date stated on the income
      tax bill (the Notice of Assessment). IRAS reviews the amendment and informs
      the taxpayer of the outcome.
    source: amend_bill
  - text: >
      The 'Amend Tax Bill' digital service may be used to revise an income
      declaration, to add or amend claims for deductions and reliefs, and to claim
      Parenthood Tax Rebate.
    source: amend_bill
  - text: >
      The obligation to pay is not suspended by an objection: tax must be paid
      within 1 month of the Notice of Assessment, and a late payment penalty
      applies to tax outstanding after 1 month, even where an objection is under
      review.
    source: amend_bill
  - text: >
      Where an assessment is revised after an objection is reviewed, any credit
      balance is refunded within 30 days from the date of the new tax bill, the
      Notice of Assessment (Amended).
    source: amend_bill
  - text: >
      The re-filing route by 18 April does not apply to taxpayers under the Direct
      Notice of Assessment (D-NOA) scheme.
    source: amend_bill

decision_steps:
  - condition: Asking about the figures in their own assessment, or the status of their own objection
    action: Escalate
    reason: account_specific
  - condition: Asking IRAS to recompute their tax, relief or revised balance
    action: Escalate
    reason: amount_computation_requested
  - condition: Asking for a penalty to be waived because of the assessment
    action: Escalate
    reason: hardship_or_waiver_request
  - condition: Asking only how or when to file a return, with no dispute about figures
    action: Route to SOP-FIL-001
    reason: tie_break_filing_mechanics
  - condition: Otherwise
    action: Explain the assessment type and the amendment route from the key facts

approved_phrasing:
  - id: noa_types
    text: >
      A Notice of Assessment (Original) is the tax bill computed from the return
      you filed together with information provided under the Auto-Inclusion
      Scheme. A Notice of Assessment (Amended) is issued when your assessment is
      revised downwards, and a Notice of Assessment (Additional) when it is
      revised upwards. A Notice of Assessment (Estimated) may be issued where a
      return has not been filed by the due date; you must still file the return so
      that the assessment can be revised.
  - id: amend_window
    text: >
      If you need to make a change after receiving your tax bill, you may file an
      amendment using the 'Amend Tax Bill' digital service at myTax Portal within
      30 days from the date on your Notice of Assessment. IRAS will review the
      amendment and inform you of the outcome.
  - id: pay_while_objecting
    text: >
      Please note that filing an objection does not defer payment. Tax is due
      within 1 month of the date of your Notice of Assessment, and a late payment
      penalty applies to tax outstanding after that date even while an objection
      is being reviewed. If your assessment is revised, any credit balance is
      refunded within 30 days from the date of the amended tax bill.
  - id: ya_meaning
    text: >
      The Year of Assessment is the year in which tax is calculated and charged on
      income earned in the preceding calendar year. For example, Year of
      Assessment 2026 covers income earned from 1 January to 31 December 2025.

do_not:
  - Do not comment on the figures in a specific taxpayer's assessment.
  - Do not predict the outcome of an objection or amendment.
  - Do not recompute tax, reliefs or a revised balance.
  - Do not advise that payment may be withheld pending an objection.

related:

  - SOP-PAY-002   # payment due date and late-payment penalties
  - SOP-REL-005   # relief cap — HELD OUT, see sop_design.md S5

# SOP-RES-001 — Handling residency enquiries
#
# Class: residency (auto_answerable).
#
# BOUNDARY NOTE: a Certificate of Residence exists in order to claim DTA
# benefits, and `foreign_income_dta` is a HELD-OUT class (sop_design.md S5).
# This SOP therefore covers *how to obtain a COR* and *what the residency test
# is*, and stops at the DTA boundary. An enquiry about whether particular
# foreign income is taxable, or how DTA relief applies, is `foreign_income_dta`
# and escalates as `no_supporting_sop`. Keeping the seam explicit is what makes
# the holdout produce a genuinely unanswerable case rather than a near-miss.

title: Handling residency enquiries
version: "1.0"
effective_date: 2026-01-01
supersedes: null
applies_to_ya: [2025, 2026]
intents: [residency]
indexed: true
owner_queue: IIT-General          # INVENTED — not a real IRAS queue

scope: >
  Taxpayer asks whether they are a tax resident, how the residency test works,
  how non-residents are taxed, or how to obtain a Certificate of Residence.

not_in_scope:
  - text: Confirming this particular taxpayer's residency status for a given YA.
    route_to: account_specific
  - text: Whether specific foreign income is taxable, or how DTA relief applies to it.
    route_to: foreign_income_dta             # HELD OUT — yields no_supporting_sop
  - text: Computing tax at resident or non-resident rates for the taxpayer.
    route_to: amount_computation_requested

    route_to: oos_other_agency

facts:
  - text: >
      An individual is treated as a tax resident for a Year of Assessment if they
      are a Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident who resides in
      Singapore except for temporary absences.
    source: rates
  - text: >
      A foreigner is treated as a tax resident if they have stayed or worked in
      Singapore for at least 183 days in the previous calendar year.
    source: rates
  - text: >
      A foreigner is also treated as a tax resident if they have stayed or worked
      in Singapore continuously for 3 consecutive years, even if the period of
      stay was less than 183 days in the first and/or third year.
    source: rates
  - text: >
      A foreigner who has worked in Singapore for a continuous period straddling
      2 calendar years, with a total period of stay of at least 183 days, is
      treated as a tax resident. This applies to employees who entered Singapore
      but excludes company directors, public entertainers and professionals.
    source: rates
  - text: >
      An individual who does not meet the residency conditions is treated as a
      non-resident for tax purposes.
    source: rates
  - text: >
      Resident tax rates are progressive; the current highest personal income tax
      rate is 24%.
    source: rates
  - text: >
      Employment income of a non-resident individual is taxed at a flat rate of
      15%, or at the progressive resident rates, whichever produces the higher
      tax amount.
    source: rates
  - text: >
      The tax rate for non-resident individuals on director's fees, consultation
      fees and all other income is currently 24%. This applies to all income
      including rental income, pension and director's fees, except employment
      income and certain income taxable at reduced withholding rates.
    source: rates
  - text: >
      Before YA 2024 the rate for non-resident individuals was 22%, except on
      employment income.
    source: rates

      A Certificate of Residence (COR) is a letter certifying that the taxpayer is
      a tax resident in Singapore, for the purpose of claiming benefits under

    source: cor
  - text: >
      A COR must be submitted to the foreign tax authority to prove Singapore tax
      residency; non-tax-residents do not enjoy DTA benefits.
    source: cor
  - text: A COR application is processed in 2 to 3 weeks.
    source: cor
  - text: >
      Where notification preferences are set to digital notices, the taxpayer is
      notified by SMS and/or email when the certification letter is ready for
      viewing at myTax Portal.
    source: cor

decision_steps:
  - condition: Asking IRAS to confirm their own residency status for a given year
    action: Escalate
    reason: account_specific
  - condition: Asking whether particular foreign income is taxable, or how DTA relief applies
    action: Escalate
    reason: foreign_income_dta
  - condition: Asking IRAS to compute tax at resident or non-resident rates
    action: Escalate
    reason: amount_computation_requested
  - condition: Asking about tax clearance for a departing employee
    action: Redirect
    reason: oos_other_agency
  - condition: Otherwise

approved_phrasing:
  - id: residency_test
    text: >
      You will be treated as a tax resident for a Year of Assessment if you are a
      Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident residing in Singapore apart from
      temporary absences, or if you are a foreigner who has stayed or worked in
      Singapore for at least 183 days in the previous calendar year. You are also
      treated as a tax resident if you have stayed or worked here continuously for
      3 consecutive years, or worked here for a continuous period straddling 2
      calendar years with a total stay of at least 183 days. If you do not meet
      these conditions you are treated as a non-resident for tax purposes.
  - id: non_resident_rates
    text: >
      Employment income of a non-resident is taxed at a flat rate of 15% or at the
      progressive resident rates, whichever gives the higher amount of tax. Other
      income, including director's fees, consultation fees, rental income and
      pension, is taxed at 24%.
  - id: cor
    text: >
      A Certificate of Residence certifies that you are a Singapore tax resident,
      so that you can claim benefits under an Avoidance of Double Taxation
      Agreement with a foreign jurisdiction. Applications are processed in 2 to 3
      weeks, and you will be notified when the letter is ready for viewing at
      myTax Portal.

do_not:
  - Do not confirm a specific taxpayer's residency status.
  - Do not count a specific taxpayer's days of presence for them.
  - Do not compute tax at either resident or non-resident rates.
  - Do not advise on whether particular foreign income is taxable, or on how DTA
    relief applies — escalate instead.

  - SOP-RTE-002   # tax clearance and other agencies
  - SOP-FIL-001   # non-residents' obligation to file

      temporary absences, or if you are a foreigner who has stayed or worked in
      Singapore for at least 183 days in the previous calendar year. You are also
      treated as a tax resident if you have stayed or worked here continuously for
      3 consecutive years, or worked here for a continuous period straddling 2
      calendar years with a total stay of at least 183 days. If you do not meet
      these conditions you are treated as a non-resident for tax purposes.

    text: >

...mount of WMCR you can claim is based on the date your child became a Singapore Citizen. You may claim WMCR in your tax filing for YA 2026 even if your child has passed away in 2025. If your child was born or adopted before 1 Jan 2024 but became a Singapore Citizen only after 1 Jan 2024, the fixed dollar rate of WMCR will apply to you. Determining child order The amount of relief varies for each child based on the child order in the family unit. The order of your child is based on: For a child born to you and your spouse/ex-spouse Date of birth shown in your child's birth certificate For a child born to you and your spouse/ex-spouse before you are married to your spouse/ex-spouse Date of marriage For a step-child Date of birth shown in your child's birth certificate For a legally adopted child Date of legal adoption as shown in the adoption papers A deceased/ stillborn child ^ is counted in determining the order of children. ^ Applicable from YA 2022 onwards for WMCR claims, where the married woman, divorcee or widow claiming the deduction is the natural mother of the stillborn child. Amount of relief The amount of WMCR that you may claim for each child is based on the child order. This is then matched to a fixed dollar tax relief. The table below explains how the WMCR amount is calculated: Child order Qualifying Singaporean child born/adopted on or after 1 Jan 2024 Working Mother's Child Relief amount Qualifying Singaporean child born/adopted before 1 Jan 2024 Working Mother's Child Relief amount 1st $8,000 15% of mother's earned income 2nd $10,000 20% of mother's earned income 3rd and beyond $12,000 25% of mother's earned income As part of the review of the Government�s support for Marriage and Parenthood , (PDF, 385KB) with effect from YA 2025, the WMCR will be changed from a percentage of an eligible working mother�s annual earned income to a fixed dollar tax relief for Singaporean children born or adopted on or after 1 Jan 2024. If a mother claims WMCR for multiple children, the WMCR allowed for each child are added together and the total claim is capped at 100% of her earned income. Please note that a personal income tax relief cap of $80,000 applies to the total amount of all tax reliefs claimed for each YA. Example 1: Claiming WMCR on 2 children Mrs Heng had an earned income of $100,000 in 2025. Her first child started working in 2025 and received an annual income exceeding $8,000. Mrs Heng�s second child was below 16 and studying full-time in 2025. The amount of WMCR that Mrs Heng may claim for YA 2026 is: Child order WMCR amount based on Mrs Heng's earned income of $100,000 WMCR allowable ($) Cumulative WMCR allowable ($) 1st $15,000 (15% x $100,000) Nil Nil No WMCR is allowed on her first child as the child had income exceeding $8,000 in 2025 2nd $20,000 (20% x $100,000) 20,000 20,000 (20% of her earned income) Example 2: Claiming WMCR on children born before and after 1 Jan 2024 Mrs Teo had an earned income of $90,000 in 2025. Her first child is 4 years old and her second child was born in 2024. The amount of WMCR that Mrs Teo may claim for YA 2026 is: Child order WMCR amount based on Mrs Teo's earned income of $90,000 WMCR allowable ($) Cumulative WMCR allowable ($) 1st $13,500 (15% x $90,000) 13,500 13,500 (15% of her earned income) 2nd $10,000 (based on WMCR allowable for qualifying child born on or after 1 Jan 2024 with child order 2) 10,000 13,500 + 10,000 = 23,500 Claiming other reliefs on the same child You may claim WMCR even if you and/or your husband or ex-husband has already claimed QCR/ Child Relief (Disability) on the same child. However, you must satisfy the following conditions: QCR/Child Relief (Disability) claims will be allowed first (it does not matter whether the claim is made by you or your husband/ex-husband); The total Child Relief cap (i.e. QCR/Child Relief (Disability) plus WMCR) is $50,000 per child ; and The WMCR is limited to the remaining balance after the QCR/Child Relief (Disability) claim is allowed. Example 3: Claiming WMCR on children for whom your husband/ex-husband has claimed other child reliefs Mr and Mrs Lim have 2 children, aged 16 and 17 respectively. Their first child is physically disabled. Mr Lim has claimed the full amount of Child Relief (Disability) for the first child and QCR for the second child. Mrs Lim earned an income of $250,000 in 2025. Apart from Earned Income Relief of $1,000 and WMCR, Mrs Lim is not claiming any other personal reliefs for the YA 2026. Mrs Lim�s WMCR claim: Child order WMCR amount based on Mrs Lim's earned income of $250,000 QCR/Child Relief (Disability) claimed by Mr Lim ($) WMCR claimed by Mrs Lim ($) Cumulative WMCR claimed by Mrs Lim ($) 1st $37,500 (15% x $250,000) 7,500 (Child Relief (Disability)) 37,500 37,500 2nd $50,000 (20% x $250,000) 4,000 (QCR) 46,000 ! 37,500 + 46,000 = 83,500 Total personal reliefs allowed to Mrs Lim = $80,000 (i.e. Personal income tax relief cap of $80,000 applies) ! QCR/Child Relief (Disability) + WMCR is subject to a cap of $50,000 per child. Example 4: Claiming Parenthood Tax Rebate (PTR) and WMCR Mr and Mrs Chen's first child was born in 2025. Mrs Chen was working and had an earned income of $80,000 for that year. They decided that Mrs Chen would claim the full amount of QCR of $4,000. Mr and Mrs Chen are Singapore tax residents for YA 2026 and are entitled to PTR of $5,000 for their first child. They have agreed to share the amount of PTR equally (i.e. $2,500 each). This is the single most important fact set in the corpus. The **1 Jan 2024 born/adopted split** (fixed dollar vs percentage of earned income) is a genuine, real supersession — better than the invented one S10.1 proposed. I'll use it.

Let me write the relief specs.

# SOP-REL-001 — Qualifying Child Relief and Child Relief (Disability)
#
# Class: tax_reliefs (auto_answerable). One of FOUR indexed SOPs in this class,
# so within-group selection by the drafter is measurable here (sop_design.md S6).
#
# COMPUTATION BOUNDARY: QCR interacts with WMCR through an ordering rule and a
# per-child cap (REL-004), and the total is then subject to the $80,000 personal
# relief cap (REL-005, HELD OUT). Stating eligibility is safe; arithmetic is not.
# This is the failure mode the whole design exists to prevent — sop_design.md S11.

sop_id: SOP-REL-001
title: Qualifying Child Relief and Child Relief (Disability)
version: "1.0"
effective_date: 2026-01-01
supersedes: null
applies_to_ya: [2025, 2026]
intents: [tax_reliefs]
indexed: true
owner_queue: IIT-General          # INVENTED — not a real IRAS queue
handling_target: 5_working_days   # ILLUSTRATIVE — not a real IRAS SLA
auto_reply_permitted: true
escalate_if:
  - account_specific
  - amount_computation_requested

references:
  - id: qcr
    url: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/qualifying-child-relief-(qcr)-child-relief-(disability)
    fetched: 2026-09-01

scope: >
  Taxpayer asks whether they qualify for Qualifying Child Relief or Child Relief
  (Disability), what the conditions are, how the relief is shared between parents,
  or how to claim it.

not_in_scope:
  - text: How much relief this taxpayer will receive, or their resulting tax.
    route_to: amount_computation_requested
  - text: Whether a claim already made has been allowed.
    route_to: account_specific
  - text: How WMCR interacts with QCR, and the per-child cap.
    route_to: tax_reliefs                    # -> SOP-REL-004, same class
  - text: Whether the total of all reliefs is limited.
    route_to: tax_reliefs                    # -> SOP-REL-005, HELD OUT

facts:
  - text: >
      To claim Qualifying Child Relief for Year of Assessment 2026, all conditions
      must be satisfied in 2025.
    source: qcr
  - text: >
      The child must be unmarried, and must be born to the taxpayer and their
      spouse or ex-spouse, be a step-child, or be legally adopted.
    source: qcr
  - text: >
      The child must have been below 16 years old, or 16 years old or above and
      studying full-time at any university, college or other educational
      institution at any time in the year.
    source: qcr
  - text: >
      The child must not have had annual income exceeding $8,000 in the year. For
      YA 2024 and before, the annual income threshold was $4,000.
    source: qcr
  - text: Qualifying Child Relief is $4,000 per qualifying child.
    source: qcr
  - text: Child Relief (Disability) is $7,500 per qualifying child.
    source: qcr
  - text: >
      Where a working mother has met the conditions for Working Mother's Child
      Relief, QCR or Child Relief (Disability) and WMCR may both be claimed on the
      same child.
    source: qcr
  - text: >
      QCR or Child Relief (Disability) plus WMCR is capped at $50,000 per child.
    source: qcr
  - text: >
      QCR or Child Relief (Disability) is allowed first, regardless of whether it
      is claimed by the father or the mother, and WMCR is limited to the remaining
      balance.
    source: qcr
  - text: >
      Parents may share the relief on the same child according to an apportionment
      they agree between themselves.
    source: qcr

decision_steps:
  - condition: Asking how much relief they will get, or what their tax will be
    action: Escalate
    reason: amount_computation_requested
  - condition: Asking whether their own claim was allowed, or about their own tax bill
    action: Escalate
    reason: account_specific
  - condition: Asking specifically about the WMCR interaction or the per-child cap
    action: Also ground on SOP-REL-004
  - condition: Asking whether total reliefs are capped
    action: Escalate
    reason: no_supporting_sop                # REL-005 is held out
  - condition: Otherwise
    action: State the qualifying conditions from the key facts

approved_phrasing:
  - id: qcr_conditions
    text: >
      To claim Qualifying Child Relief for Year of Assessment 2026, all the
      conditions must have been met in 2025. Your child must be unmarried, and
      must be your own child, a step-child, or legally adopted. The child must
      have been below 16 years old, or 16 or above and studying full-time at a
      university, college or other educational institution at any time during the
      year. The child must also not have had annual income of more than $8,000.
  - id: qcr_amounts
    text: >
      Qualifying Child Relief is $4,000 per qualifying child, and Child Relief
      (Disability) is $7,500 per qualifying child.
  - id: sharing
    text: >
      Parents may share the relief for the same child in a proportion they agree
      between themselves.
  - id: wmcr_ordering
    text: >
      If you are a working mother who also qualifies for Working Mother's Child
      Relief, both reliefs may be claimed on the same child. Qualifying Child
      Relief or Child Relief (Disability) is allowed first, and Working Mother's
      Child Relief is limited to the remaining balance, with a combined cap of
      $50,000 per child.
  - id: computation_escalation
    text: >
      The amount of relief you will actually receive depends on how these reliefs
      interact and on the overall cap on personal reliefs, so we have passed your
      enquiry to an officer who will confirm the position for your circumstances.

do_not:
  - Do not compute a relief amount, a combined relief total, or resulting tax.
  - Do not confirm whether a specific claim has been allowed.
  - Do not state the overall personal relief cap — that is SOP-REL-005, which is
    not available to this procedure. Escalate instead.
  - Do not advise on how parents should apportion relief between themselves.

related:
  - SOP-REL-004   # WMCR and PTR — the ordering rule and the $50,000 per-child cap
  - SOP-REL-005   # personal income tax relief cap — HELD OUT (sop_design.md S5)
  - SOP-ASM-001   # amending a relief claim after the tax bill

# SOP-REL-002 — Parent Relief and Parent Relief (Disability)
#
# Class: tax_reliefs (auto_answerable). Second of four indexed relief SOPs.

sop_id: SOP-REL-002
title: Parent Relief and Parent Relief (Disability)
version: "1.0"
effective_date: 2026-01-01
supersedes: null
applies_to_ya: [2025, 2026]
intents: [tax_reliefs]
indexed: true
owner_queue: IIT-General          # INVENTED — not a real IRAS queue
handling_target: 5_working_days   # ILLUSTRATIVE — not a real IRAS SLA
auto_reply_permitted: true
escalate_if:
  - account_specific
  - amount_computation_requested

references:
  - id: parent_relief
    url: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/parent-relief-parent-relief-(disability)
    fetched: 2026-09-01

scope: >
  Taxpayer asks whether they qualify for Parent Relief or Parent Relief
  (Disability) in respect of a parent, grandparent, parent-in-law or
  grandparent-in-law, what the conditions are, how many dependants may be
  claimed, or how the relief is shared between claimants.

not_in_scope:
  - text: How much relief this taxpayer will receive, or their resulting tax.
    route_to: amount_computation_requested
  - text: Whether a claim already made has been allowed.
    route_to: account_specific
  - text: Whether the total of all reliefs is limited.
    route_to: tax_reliefs                    # -> SOP-REL-005, HELD OUT

facts:
  - text: >
      Parent Relief recognises individuals supporting their parents,
      grandparents, parents-in-law or grandparents-in-law in Singapore.
    source: parent_relief
  - text: >
      Qualifying dependants include parents, parents-in-law, grandparents,
      grandparents-in-law, step-parents, step-grandparents, adoptive parents and
      adoptive grandparents.
    source: parent_relief
  - text: The dependant must have been 55 years of age or above.
    source: parent_relief
  - text: >
      The dependant must not have had annual income of more than $8,000 in 2025.
      For YA 2024 and before, the threshold was $4,000.
    source: parent_relief
  - text: >
      The dependant must have been living with the taxpayer in the same household
      in Singapore, or otherwise meet the alternative residence condition.
    source: parent_relief
  - text: >
      Where the dependant did not live with the taxpayer, the relief applies only
      if the dependant stayed in Singapore for at least 8 months in 2025.
    source: parent_relief
  - text: >
      Parent Relief is $9,000 per dependant where the taxpayer stays with the
      dependant, and $5,500 per dependant where they do not.
    source: parent_relief
  - text: >
      Parent Relief (Disability) is $14,000 per dependant where the taxpayer stays
      with the dependant, and $10,000 per dependant where they do not.
    source: parent_relief
  - text: >
      Parent Relief or Parent Relief (Disability) may be claimed for up to 2
      dependants.
    source: parent_relief
  - text: >
      Where more than one individual maintains the same dependant and each meets
      the qualifying conditions, the relief may be shared between the claimants.
    source: parent_relief

decision_steps:
  - condition: Asking how much relief they will get, or what their tax will be
    action: Escalate
    reason: amount_computation_requested
  - condition: Asking whether their own claim was allowed
    action: Escalate
    reason: account_specific
  - condition: Asking whether total reliefs are capped
    action: Escalate
    reason: no_supporting_sop                # REL-005 is held out
  - condition: Otherwise
    action: State the qualifying conditions and the applicable rates from the key facts

approved_phrasing:
  - id: conditions
    text: >
      To claim Parent Relief you must have supported a dependant who was 55 years
      of age or above, who did not have annual income of more than $8,000 in 2025,
      and who was living with you in the same household in Singapore. If your
      dependant did not live with you, the relief applies only if they stayed in
      Singapore for at least 8 months in the year. Qualifying dependants include
      parents, grandparents, parents-in-law and grandparents-in-law, as well as
      step-parents and adoptive parents.
  - id: amounts
    text: >
      Parent Relief is $9,000 per dependant if you stay with your dependant, and
      $5,500 if you do not. Parent Relief (Disability) is $14,000 per dependant if
      you stay with your dependant, and $10,000 if you do not.
  - id: number_and_sharing
    text: >
      You may claim the relief for up to 2 dependants. If more than one person
      supports the same dependant and each meets the qualifying conditions, the
      relief may be shared between you.

do_not:
  - Do not compute a relief amount or the resulting tax.
  - Do not confirm whether a specific claim has been allowed.
  - Do not state the overall personal relief cap — escalate instead.
  - Do not advise claimants on how to apportion a shared claim between themselves.

related:
  - SOP-REL-005   # personal income tax relief cap — HELD OUT (sop_design.md S5)
  - SOP-ASM-001   # amending a relief claim after the tax bill

# SOP-REL-003 — CPF and SRS reliefs
#
# Class: tax_reliefs (auto_answerable). Third of four indexed relief SOPs.
#
# NOTE: the source pages for both CPF and SRS relief mention the $80,000 personal
# relief cap in passing. That fact is deliberately NOT restated here — it belongs
# to SOP-REL-005, which is held out (sop_design.md S5). Repeating it would defeat
# the partial-answer holdout, since the agent could answer the cap question from
# an indexed SOP. Correct behaviour is to state eligibility and escalate the cap.

sop_id: SOP-REL-003
title: CPF and SRS reliefs
version: "1.0"
effective_date: 2026-01-01
supersedes: null
applies_to_ya: [2025, 2026]
intents: [tax_reliefs]
indexed: true
owner_queue: IIT-General          # INVENTED — not a real IRAS queue
handling_target: 5_working_days   # ILLUSTRATIVE — not a real IRAS SLA
auto_reply_permitted: true
escalate_if:
  - account_specific
  - amount_computation_requested

references:
  - id: cpf_relief
    url: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/central-provident-fund(cpf)-relief-for-employees
    fetched: 2026-09-01
  - id: srs_relief
    url: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/special-tax-schemes/srs-contributions
    fetched: 2026-09-01

scope: >
  Taxpayer asks which CPF contributions qualify for relief, which do not, how SRS
  contributions attract relief, or what the yearly SRS contribution caps are.

not_in_scope:
  - text: The amount of CPF or SRS relief this taxpayer will receive.
    route_to: amount_computation_requested
  - text: The taxpayer's own CPF contribution records or SRS account balance.
    route_to: account_specific
  - text: CPF scheme matters that are not tax relief — contribution rates, withdrawal rules, account balances.
    route_to: oos_other_agency               # CPF Board, not IRAS
  - text: Whether the total of all reliefs is limited.
    route_to: tax_reliefs                    # -> SOP-REL-005, HELD OUT

facts:
  - text: >
      Compulsory employee CPF contributions under the CPF Act, or contributions to
      an approved pension or provident fund, qualify for CPF relief.
    source: cpf_relief
  - text: Voluntary contributions to a MediSave Account qualify for CPF relief.
    source: cpf_relief
  - text: >
      Voluntary contributions made in excess of the compulsory contributions under
      the CPF Act are not eligible for relief.
    source: cpf_relief
  - text: >
      CPF contributions on additional wages that exceed the CPF cap on wages from
      related employers are not eligible for relief.
    source: cpf_relief
  - text: >
      CPF contributions made in respect of overseas employment are not eligible
      for relief.
    source: cpf_relief
  - text: >
      There is no refund for accepted voluntary CPF contributions, so a taxpayer
      should evaluate whether they would benefit from the relief before
      contributing.
    source: cpf_relief
  - text: >
      The Supplementary Retirement Scheme is a voluntary scheme encouraging
      individuals to save for retirement over and above their CPF savings.
    source: srs_relief
  - text: >
      The yearly maximum SRS contribution is $15,300 for Singapore Citizens and
      Singapore Permanent Residents, and $35,700 for foreigners.
    source: srs_relief
  - text: >
      A foreigner must declare their foreigner status to the SRS bank operator
      yearly, so that the operator can calculate the maximum SRS contribution.
    source: srs_relief
  - text: >
      Opening SRS accounts with more than one SRS operator is an offence and a
      penalty may be imposed.
    source: srs_relief
  - text: >
      A taxpayer should check with their SRS bank operator for the cut-off date
      for SRS contributions.
    source: srs_relief

decision_steps:
  - condition: Asking how much CPF or SRS relief they will receive
    action: Escalate
    reason: amount_computation_requested
  - condition: Asking about their own contribution records or account balance
    action: Escalate
    reason: account_specific
  - condition: Asking about CPF contribution rates, withdrawals or balances rather than tax relief
    action: Redirect to CPF Board
    reason: oos_other_agency
  - condition: Asking whether total reliefs are capped
    action: Escalate
    reason: no_supporting_sop                # REL-005 is held out
  - condition: Otherwise
    action: State which contributions qualify, and the SRS caps, from the key facts

approved_phrasing:
  - id: cpf_qualifying
    text: >
      Compulsory employee CPF contributions made under the CPF Act, contributions
      to an approved pension or provident fund, and voluntary contributions to
      your MediSave Account qualify for CPF relief.
  - id: cpf_not_qualifying
    text: >
      Voluntary contributions in excess of the compulsory contributions under the
      CPF Act do not qualify for relief. Neither do CPF contributions on
      additional wages exceeding the CPF wage cap from related employers, or
      contributions made in respect of overseas employment. Please note that
      accepted voluntary CPF contributions cannot be refunded.
  - id: srs_caps
    text: >
      The Supplementary Retirement Scheme is a voluntary scheme for retirement
      savings over and above CPF. The yearly maximum contribution is $15,300 for
      Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents, and $35,700 for foreigners. If
      you are a foreigner, you need to declare your status to your SRS operator
      each year so that they can calculate your contribution cap.
  - id: cpf_board_redirect
    text: >
      Questions about CPF contribution rates, withdrawals or your account balance
      are handled by the CPF Board rather than IRAS. Please contact the CPF Board
      directly at cpf.gov.sg.

do_not:
  - Do not compute a relief amount or the resulting tax.
  - Do not confirm a taxpayer's own contribution or account figures.
  - Do not state the overall personal relief cap — escalate instead.
  - Do not advise whether a voluntary contribution is financially worthwhile.
  - Do not answer CPF scheme questions that belong to the CPF Board.

related:
  - SOP-REL-005   # personal income tax relief cap — HELD OUT (sop_design.md S5)
  - SOP-RTE-002   # CPF Board and other agencies

# percentage of the mother's earned income to a fixed dollar relief for Singaporean
# children born or adopted on or after 1 Jan 2024. Children born before that date

# exactly what `applies_to_ya` plus this note exist to test.

# the balance), the $50,000 per-child cap, and PTR carry-forward. All three are
# arithmetic. State them as rules; never apply them.

title: Working Mother's Child Relief and Parenthood Tax Rebate
version: "2.0"
effective_date: 2025-01-01
supersedes: SOP-REL-004-v1.0
applies_to_ya: [2025, 2026]
intents: [tax_reliefs]

    fetched: 2026-09-01

    fetched: 2026-09-01

scope: >
  Taxpayer asks whether they qualify for Working Mother's Child Relief, how the

not_in_scope:
  - text: How much WMCR or PTR this taxpayer will receive, or their resulting tax.
    route_to: amount_computation_requested

  - text: >

      working mother's annual earned income to a fixed dollar tax relief, for
      Singaporean children born or adopted on or after 1 January 2024.
    source: wmcr
  - text: >
      For a qualifying Singaporean child born or adopted on or after 1 January
      2024, WMCR is $8,000 for the first child, $10,000 for the second, and
      $12,000 for the third and each subsequent child.
    source: wmcr
  - text: >
      For a qualifying Singaporean child born or adopted before 1 January 2024,
      WMCR is 15% of the mother's earned income for the first child, 20% for the
      second, and 25% for the third and each subsequent child.
    source: wmcr
  - text: >
      Where a child was born or adopted before 1 January 2024 but became a
      Singapore Citizen only after that date, the fixed dollar rate applies. The
      amount is based on the date the child became a Singapore Citizen.
    source: wmcr
  - text: >
      Child order is determined by date of birth for a child born to the taxpayer
      and their spouse or ex-spouse; by date of marriage where the child was born
      before the marriage; by date of birth for a step-child; and by the date of
      legal adoption for an adopted child.
    source: wmcr
  - text: >
      A deceased or stillborn child is counted in determining the order of
      children.
    source: wmcr
  - text: >
      Where a mother claims WMCR for multiple children, the amounts are added
      together and the total claim is capped at 100% of her earned income.
    source: wmcr
  - text: >
      WMCR may be claimed even where the taxpayer or her husband or ex-husband has
      already claimed QCR or Child Relief (Disability) on the same child.
    source: wmcr
  - text: >
      QCR or Child Relief (Disability) is allowed first, and WMCR is limited to
      the remaining balance. The combined cap is $50,000 per child.
    source: wmcr
  - text: >
      WMCR may be claimed for YA 2026 even where the child passed away in 2025.
    source: wmcr
  - text: >
      Parenthood Tax Rebate is given to tax residents, is a one-off rebate of up to
      $20,000 per child, and may be claimed on a qualifying child only once.
    source: ptr
  - text: >
      PTR amounts by child order are $5,000 for the first child, $10,000 for the
      second, and $20,000 for the third and fourth child.
    source: ptr
  - text: >
      Any unutilised PTR is carried forward to offset income tax payable in
      subsequent years until it is fully utilised.
    source: ptr
  - text: >
      Unutilised PTR may be transferred to a spouse, and where one spouse passes
      away the surviving spouse may continue to use the credit balance remaining
      in their respective PTR accounts.
    source: ptr
  - text: >
      For PTR purposes no child is considered a member of two households, and
      children from a previous marriage are taken into account in determining
      child order.
    source: ptr

decision_steps:
  - condition: Asking how much WMCR or PTR they will get, or what their tax will be

    reason: amount_computation_requested
  - condition: Asking about their own PTR balance, or whether their claim was allowed
    action: Escalate
    reason: account_specific
  - condition: Child born or adopted on or after 1 Jan 2024 (or became a Singapore Citizen after that date)
    action: Apply the fixed dollar basis
  - condition: Child born or adopted before 1 Jan 2024

    action: Escalate
    reason: no_supporting_sop                # REL-005 is held out
  - condition: Otherwise
    action: State the qualifying basis and the ordering rule from the key facts

  - id: wmcr_post_2024
    text: >
      For a qualifying Singaporean child born or adopted on or after 1 January

      child, $10,000 for the second, and $12,000 for the third and each subsequent
      child.

    text: >
      For a qualifying Singaporean child born or adopted before 1 January 2024,

      and each subsequent child.

    text: >

      and Working Mother's Child Relief is limited to the remaining balance, with a
      combined cap of $50,000 per child.
  - id: ptr
    text: >
      The Parenthood Tax Rebate is a one-off rebate for tax residents, of $5,000
      for the first child, $10,000 for the second, and $20,000 for the third and
      fourth child. Any unutilised amount is carried forward to offset your income
      tax in later years until it is fully used, and it may also be transferred to

  - id: computation_escalation
    text: >
      Because these reliefs interact with one another and are subject to caps, we
      have passed your enquiry to an officer who will confirm the amounts that
      apply to your circumstances.

  - Do not compute a WMCR amount, a PTR balance, or resulting tax.
  - Do not apply the percentage basis to a child born on or after 1 Jan 2024, or

# SOP-REL-005 — Personal income tax relief cap
#
# Class: tax_reliefs. ***HELD OUT — indexed: false*** (sop_design.md S5).
#
# This is the PARTIAL-ANSWER holdout, and it is a different kind from INC-001 and
# INC-002. Those hold out a whole class, so the email is unanswerable and the
# router escalates on `no_supporting_sop`. REL-005 holds out ONE SOP from an
# otherwise-indexed class: `tax_reliefs` still resolves to REL-001..004, so the
# router sees a populated SOP list and does NOT fire `no_supporting_sop`.
#
# The correct behaviour is therefore subtler than "escalate": the agent can state
# relief eligibility from the indexed SOPs, but cannot reason about the $80,000
# cap. What it must not do is produce a confident total. Every indexed relief SOP
# carries a matching `do_not` forbidding it from stating the cap, and routes the
# question to escalation instead.
#
# The SOP is authored in full so that (a) the holdout is a matter of excluding a
# file from the index rather than an arbitrary cut, and (b) re-indexing it later
# requires no code change — flip `indexed` to true.

sop_id: SOP-REL-005
title: Personal income tax relief cap
version: "1.0"
effective_date: 2026-01-01
supersedes: null
applies_to_ya: [2025, 2026]
intents: [tax_reliefs]
indexed: false                    # HELD OUT — excluded from the index
owner_queue: IIT-General          # INVENTED — not a real IRAS queue
handling_target: 5_working_days   # ILLUSTRATIVE — not a real IRAS SLA
auto_reply_permitted: true
escalate_if:
  - account_specific
  - amount_computation_requested

references:
  - id: relief_cap
    url: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs
    fetched: 2026-09-01
  - id: wmcr
    url: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/working-mother's-child-relief-(wmcr)
    fetched: 2026-09-01

scope: >
  Taxpayer asks whether there is a limit on the total amount of personal reliefs
  they may claim, how the cap applies across different reliefs, or what happens
  when their claims exceed it.

not_in_scope:
  - text: Whether this taxpayer's own reliefs exceed the cap, and by how much.
    route_to: account_specific
  - text: Computing the taxpayer's total reliefs or resulting tax.
    route_to: amount_computation_requested

facts:
  - text: >
      A personal income tax relief cap of $80,000 applies to the total amount of
      all tax reliefs claimed for each Year of Assessment.
    source: relief_cap
  - text: >
      A taxpayer is affected by the cap if the total amount of personal reliefs
      they claim exceeds $80,000.
    source: relief_cap
  - text: >
      Where the cap applies, the reliefs allowed are limited to $80,000, and this
      is reflected in the Notice of Assessment.
    source: relief_cap
  - text: >
      The cap applies to the total of all reliefs, including relief on compulsory
      and voluntary CPF contributions.
    source: relief_cap
  - text: >
      The $80,000 cap operates on top of the individual caps within specific
      reliefs, such as the $50,000 per-child cap on QCR or Child Relief
      (Disability) combined with WMCR.
    source: wmcr
  - text: >
      There is no refund of accepted voluntary CPF or SRS contributions where the
      relief cap means they attract no tax relief.
    source: relief_cap

decision_steps:
  - condition: Asking whether their own reliefs exceed the cap
    action: Escalate
    reason: account_specific
  - condition: Asking IRAS to total their reliefs or compute the effect of the cap
    action: Escalate
    reason: amount_computation_requested
  - condition: Otherwise
    action: State the cap and how it applies from the key facts

approved_phrasing:
  - id: cap
    text: >
      A personal income tax relief cap of $80,000 applies to the total amount of
      all tax reliefs you claim in each Year of Assessment. If the total of your
      personal reliefs exceeds $80,000, the reliefs allowed to you are limited to
      $80,000, and this is reflected in your Notice of Assessment.
  - id: interaction
    text: >
      The $80,000 cap applies on top of the caps within individual reliefs, such as
      the $50,000 combined cap per child on Qualifying Child Relief and Working
      Mother's Child Relief.
  - id: no_refund
    text: >
      Please note that voluntary CPF and SRS contributions cannot be refunded if
      the relief cap means they do not attract tax relief, so it is worth
      considering the cap before making a voluntary contribution.

do_not:
  - Do not total a taxpayer's reliefs or compute the effect of the cap for them.
  - Do not confirm whether a specific taxpayer is affected by the cap.
  - Do not advise whether a voluntary contribution is financially worthwhile.

related:
  - SOP-REL-001   # QCR and Child Relief (Disability)
  - SOP-REL-002   # Parent Relief
  - SOP-REL-003   # CPF and SRS reliefs
  - SOP-REL-004   # WMCR and PTR

# otherwise-indexed class: `tax_reliefs` still resolves to REL-001..004, so the
# router sees a populated SOP list and does NOT fire `no_supporting_sop`.

# carries a matching `do_not` forbidding it from stating the cap, and routes the
# question to escalation instead.

title: Personal income tax relief cap
version: "1.0"
effective_date: 2026-01-01
supersedes: null
applies_to_ya: [2025, 2026]
intents: [tax_reliefs]
indexed: false                    # HELD OUT — excluded from the index
owner_queue: IIT-General          # INVENTED — not a real IRAS queue
handling_target: 5_working_days   # ILLUSTRATIVE — not a real IRAS SLA

escalate_if:

references:

    fetched: 2026-09-01

scope: >

not_in_scope:

      all tax reliefs claimed for each Year of Assessment.

      they claim exceeds $80,000.
    source: relief_cap

      is reflected in the Notice of Assessment.
    source: relief_cap
  - text: >
      The cap applies to the total of all reliefs, including relief on compulsory
      and voluntary CPF contributions.
    source: relief_cap

      reliefs, such as the $50,000 per-child cap on QCR or Child Relief

# cuts across every topic and structurally belongs as a flag, not a class: "what
# is the filing deadline" and "why was MY deduction reversed" differ by a
# possessive, not by subject matter. It is kept as a class for the prototype
# because a flag needs a second detector and the lexical signal is weak.
#
# Consequence accepted in review: this class will be confused with whichever topic
# the email is about, because topical vocabulary dominates the one-or-two-token
# possessive signal — and the confusion lands on the unsafe side, since a missed
# account_specific means auto-drafting about a real taxpayer's account. A lexical
# `account_specific` BACKSTOP FLAG is therefore specified below, mirroring
# `computation_requested`: it forces escalation on strong possessive signals
# regardless of the predicted class. Measured, not assumed — report its precision
# and recall alongside the computation flag.

# SOP-ESC-002 — Hardship and waiver requests
#
# Class: hardship_or_waiver. Bucket: high_consequence — ALWAYS ESCALATES.
#
# WHY THIS NEVER AUTO-REPLIES. Two reasons, and both matter.
#
# First, consequence. A taxpayer writing that they cannot pay is in financial
# distress; the outcome turns on their circumstances, and an automated "no" — or
# an automated "yes" the agency cannot honour — is a citizen-harm failure that no
# confidence score should be permitted to authorise.
#
# Second, discretion. Waiver and instalment decisions are discretionary and
# account-specific by nature. There is no rule the agent could apply correctly
# even with perfect classification.
#
# The SOP therefore states only what is publicly true about the process and the
# consequences of inaction, and hands off. Note the tension the phrasing must
# hold: the taxpayer must be told not to ignore the bill (a 5% penalty accrues
# regardless) without being told their request will succeed.

sop_id: SOP-ESC-002
title: Hardship and waiver requests
version: "1.0"
effective_date: 2026-01-01
supersedes: null
applies_to_ya: [2025, 2026]
intents: [hardship_or_waiver]
indexed: true
owner_queue: IIT-Recovery         # INVENTED — not a real IRAS queue
handling_target: 5_working_days   # ILLUSTRATIVE — not a real IRAS SLA
auto_reply_permitted: false       # -> bucket: high_consequence
escalate_if:
  - hardship_or_waiver_request
  - account_specific
  - amount_computation_requested

references:
  - id: difficulty_paying
    url: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/receive-tax-bill-pay-tax-check-refunds/experiencing-difficulties-in-paying-your-tax
    fetched: 2026-09-01
  - id: late_payment
    url: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/receive-tax-bill-pay-tax-check-refunds/late-payment-or-non-payment-of-individual-income-tax
    fetched: 2026-09-01

scope: >
  Taxpayer states they cannot pay, asks for a longer or restructured instalment
  plan, asks for a late-payment penalty or composition amount to be waived or
  reduced, or describes financial hardship, retrenchment, illness or bereavement
  in connection with a tax debt.

not_in_scope:
  - text: Generic questions about how GIRO instalments work, with no hardship stated.

#
# Class: scam_report. Bucket: high_consequence — ALWAYS ESCALATES.
#
# WHY THIS IS A CLASS AND NOT A FLAG. It was folded into a flag in an earlier

# human quickly and must not read as routine correspondence.
#
# The one exception to "escalate silently": the acknowledgement carries the
# publicly-stated verification facts, because a taxpayer who is still being
# targeted benefits from knowing immediately what genuine IRAS contact looks like.
# Those facts are public and general; they are not advice on their specific case.

sop_id: SOP-ESC-003
title: Scam and impersonation reports
version: "1.0"
effective_date: 2026-01-01
supersedes: null
applies_to_ya: [2025, 2026]
intents: [scam_report]
indexed: true
owner_queue: IIT-Integrity        # INVENTED — not a real IRAS queue

    url: https://www.iras.gov.sg/news-events/announcements/scam-advisory/phishing-email-scam

  - id: scam_refund
    url: https://www.iras.gov.sg/news-events/announcements/scam-advisory/tax-refund-scam
    fetched: 2026-09-01

scope: >
  Taxpayer reports a suspicious email, SMS, WhatsApp message, call or website
  purporting to be from IRAS; asks whether a message they received is genuine; or
  reports that they have already responded to one, disclosed information or made
  a payment.

not_in_scope:
  - text: Reporting suspected tax evasion by another person.
    route_to: oos_other_agency
  - text: A genuine IRAS notice the taxpayer disputes.
    route_to: assessment_and_amendment

facts:
  - text: >
      All IRAS correspondence on confidential tax matters is done through myTax
      Portal, and all notices and letters are deposited at mytax.iras.gov.sg.
    source: scam_advisory
  - text: >
      Taxpayers will never receive confidential tax information or tax documents
      such as tax returns, notices of assessment or tax refund letters by email or
      SMS.
    source: scam_advisory
  - text: >
      myTax Portal is a secured, personalised portal that taxpayers access using
      Singpass authentication.
    source: scam_advisory
  - text: >
      Taxpayers who have updated their mobile number or email address are notified
      by SMS or email to log in to myTax Portal to view notices or letters, rather
      than receiving the documents themselves.

      IRAS state that the recipient is eligible for a refund, and link to a
      phishing website imitating the IRAS website that asks them to select a refund
      method using debit or credit card details.

    reason: high_consequence
  - condition: Always

approved_phrasing:
  - id: acknowledgement
    text: >

      follow up with you directly. It may help to know that IRAS conducts all
      correspondence on confidential tax matters through myTax Portal at
      mytax.iras.gov.sg, which is accessed using Singpass. IRAS will never send you
      confidential tax documents such as tax returns, notices of assessment or
      refund letters by email or SMS, and will never ask for your card details in
      order to pay you a refund. If you have already provided any information or
      made a payment, please contact your bank immediately and report the matter to

  - Do not confirm or deny that a specific message, sender address or website is
    genuine — an officer must verify this.
  - Do not ask the taxpayer to forward attachments or click any link to check it.
  - Do not request Singpass credentials, card details or an NRIC by email.
  - Do not auto-reply in a way that reads as routine correspondence — this is
    time-sensitive.

related:
  - SOP-ESC-001   # account-specific enquiries
  - SOP-PAY-002   # genuine refund process

# another IRAS tax type versus another agency entirely — and a wrong redirect is a
# visible citizen-facing failure. Cost accepted: one confusable pair, ~4 fewer
# test examples per class.

#
# Class: oos_other_agency. Bucket: out_of_scope. Automated redirect counts toward

# rather than simply decline.

# SOP-INC-001 — Rental income
#
# Class: rental_income. ***HELD OUT — indexed: false*** (sop_design.md S5).
#
# WHOLE-CLASS HOLDOUT, distinct from REL-005. Because no INDEXED SOP declares
# `intents: [rental_income]`, CLASS_TO_SOPS["rental_income"] resolves EMPTY, and
# the router fires `no_supporting_sop` by derivation — it does not read a
# hand-written bucket entry (BUILD.md S5.6). One source of truth: holding out a
# further class later needs no code change.
#
# This is what makes the unanswerable case genuine rather than simulated. The
# emails are real enquiries a citizen would send, the topic is squarely individual
# income tax, and the agent still cannot answer — because the procedure is absent,
# not because the question is odd. An agent that answers this from general
# knowledge of tax has failed the test the holdout exists to set.
#
# Authored in full so re-indexing is a one-field change.

sop_id: SOP-INC-001
title: Rental income
version: "1.0"
effective_date: 2026-01-01
supersedes: null
applies_to_ya: [2025, 2026]
intents: [rental_income]
indexed: false                    # HELD OUT — excluded from the index
owner_queue: IIT-General          # INVENTED — not a real IRAS queue
handling_target: 5_working_days   # ILLUSTRATIVE — not a real IRAS SLA
auto_reply_permitted: true
escalate_if:
  - account_specific
  - amount_computation_requested

references:
  - id: rental_income
    url: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out
    fetched: 2026-09-01

scope: >
  Taxpayer asks whether rent received is taxable, when rental income must be
  declared, what expenses may be deducted, or how the simplified claim for rental
  expenses works.

not_in_scope:
  - text: The taxpayer's own declared rental figures or assessment.
    route_to: account_specific
  - text: Computing net rental income or tax for the taxpayer.
    route_to: amount_computation_requested
  - text: Property tax, which is a different tax type.
    route_to: oos_other_agency

facts:
  - text: >
      Rent payments received from renting out a property are subject to income tax
      and must be declared in the Income Tax Return.
    source: rental_income
  - text: >
      Net rental income, after deduction of allowable expenses, is subject to
      income tax.
    source: rental_income
  - text: >
      Rental income is taxable from the date it is due and payable to the property
      owner, not the date it is actually received. Rent due in 2025 but paid in
      2026 is declared for Year of Assessment 2026.
    source: rental_income
  - text: >
      Any amount recovered from insurance on a property that is rented out is
      taxable and should be reported as part of income.
    source: rental_income
  - text: >
      Under the simplified claim for rental expenses for tenanted residential
      property, deemed rental expenses calculated as 15% of gross rent are
      pre-filled in the online tax form.
    source: rental_income
  - text: >
      In addition to the 15% deemed rental expenses, property owners may still
      claim mortgage interest on the loan taken to purchase the property.
    source: rental_income
  - text: >
      The amount of taxable rental income depends on whether the property is solely
      or jointly owned.
    source: rental_income

decision_steps:
  - condition: Asking about their own declared rental figures or assessment
    action: Escalate
    reason: account_specific
  - condition: Asking IRAS to compute net rental income or tax
    action: Escalate
    reason: amount_computation_requested
  - condition: Asking about property tax rather than income tax on rent
    action: Redirect
    reason: oos_other_agency
  - condition: Otherwise
    action: State the treatment of rental income from the key facts

approved_phrasing:
  - id: taxable
    text: >
      Rent you receive from renting out your property is subject to income tax and
      must be declared in your Income Tax Return. It is the net rental income,
      after deducting allowable expenses, that is taxed.
  - id: timing
    text: >
      Rental income is taxable from the date it is due and payable to you, rather
      than the date you actually receive it. For example, rent due to you in 2025
      but paid in January 2026 is declared for Year of Assessment 2026.
  - id: simplified_expenses
    text: >
      For tenanted residential property, a simplified claim is available: deemed
      rental expenses of 15% of your gross rent are pre-filled in the online tax
      form. You may still claim mortgage interest on the loan taken to purchase the
      property in addition to the 15%.

do_not:
  - Do not compute net rental income, allowable expenses or tax payable.
  - Do not confirm a taxpayer's own declared figures.
  - Do not advise whether the simplified claim or actual expenses is more
    advantageous for a particular taxpayer.
  - Do not answer property tax questions from this procedure.

related:
  - SOP-FIL-001   # declaring the income in the return
  - SOP-RTE-002   # property tax and other tax types

# SOP-INC-002 — Foreign income and DTA relief
#
# Class: foreign_income_dta. ***HELD OUT — indexed: false*** (sop_design.md S5).
#
# Second WHOLE-CLASS HOLDOUT. As with INC-001, no indexed SOP declares
# `intents: [foreign_income_dta]`, so CLASS_TO_SOPS resolves EMPTY and the router
# derives `no_supporting_sop`.
#
# This holdout is the harder of the two, deliberately. SOP-RES-001 IS indexed and
# covers tax residency and the Certificate of Residence — and a COR exists
# precisely in order to claim DTA benefits. So a foreign-income email sits next to
# an indexed SOP that is adjacent but insufficient: the agent can say what a COR is
# and how to get one, but cannot say whether the citizen's foreign income is
# taxable or how DTA relief applies to it.
#

Committed. Here's where things stand.

## Done

**1. Taxonomy verification** — the 12 classes hold up. Four issues found; three resolved (tie-break rule, backstop flag, OOS split kept per your call), one recorded as a limitation (per-cell N in the edge-case slice is ~10, so no per-class claims about the flags).

**2. SOP corpus input layer** — all 17 specs written and validated:
- 146 facts, every one citing a public IRAS URL, zero unresolved citations
- All facts verified against live pages fetched into gitignored `.scratch/`
- Structure matches the design exactly: `tax_reliefs`→4, `payment`→2, two classes resolving empty so `no_supporting_sop` derives correctly

Three things came out better than designed, because the live pages had more than the draft assumed:
- **The supersession is real, not invented.** WMCR genuinely changed on 1 Jan 2024 from percentage-of-earned-income to fixed dollar, and both bases are live simultaneously depending on the child's birth date. Better than the hypothetical S10.1 proposed.
- **The `foreign_income_dta` holdout is a genuine near-miss.** A Certificate of Residence exists *in order to* claim DTA benefits, and RES-001 is indexed — so the agent has adjacent-but-insufficient knowledge, which is a much stronger test than an obviously off-topic question.
- **The relief cap holdout is enforced.** The $80,000 cap appears on the CPF and WMCR pages, so I deliberately did *not* restate it in REL-003/004 — otherwise the agent could answer the cap question from an indexed SOP and the partial-answer case would collapse.

I also noticed you'd built the PII scrubber and tests in parallel, so I staged only my own files — your work is untouched and unstaged.

**Schemas → emails** and **the classifier** are still ahead. The gate before them is `generate_sops.py` (specs → `data/sop/*.md`) plus `config/taxonomy.yaml` derived from the corpus — build stages 1 and 1b.

content.text:
Verified. Answering both parts:

## Is the cap applicable to all reliefs?

**Yes — it's a global cap.** The authoritative wording:

> "A personal income tax relief cap of **$80,000** applies to the **total amount of all tax reliefs** claimed for each Year of Assessment (YA)."

> "If the total amount of reliefs claimed exceeds the relief cap, the tax reliefs will be capped at $80,000."

It applies across all 13 personal reliefs (in force from **YA 2018**), and the worked example on the page shows it biting on a *sum* — Earned Income + CPF + NSman Wife + WMCR across three children = $86,650, capped down to $80,000.

So it's not a property of CPF or WMCR. It's a property of the **total**.

## I was wrong about where it appears

My earlier statement — "it appears on the CPF and WMCR pages" — was too narrow. It's on **6 of 8** relief pages I fetched:

| Page | Mentions |
|---|---|
| tax reliefs index (`relief_cap`) | 12 |
| CPF relief | 6 |
| WMCR | 6 |
| SRS relief | 4 |
| QCR | 3 |
| PTR | 3 |
| Parent relief | 0 |
| reliefs overview | 0 |

IRAS repeats it as a warning on most individual relief pages, precisely because it's global and a taxpayer reading one page needs to know their total is constrained.

## What this means for the holdout — and it's a real problem

This strengthens the design rationale but **breaks my REL-002 spec**.

The rationale gets stronger: a global cap is exactly the right thing to hold out, because it's the one fact that can't be derived from any single relief's rules. It's a property of the sum. That's what makes REL-005 a genuine *partial-answer* case — the agent can state eligibility per relief and still cannot state the total.

But my leakage-avoidance was inconsistent. I suppressed the cap in REL-001, REL-003 and REL-004 (with explicit `do_not` lines) — but **REL-002 has no `do_not` line about the cap**, because I'd written it from the parent-relief page, which is one of the two pages that doesn't mention the cap. So the suppression is accidental there rather than deliberate, and the spec doesn't record the rule.

Let me fix that.

input.command:
cd "C:/Users/<USER>/Documents/all ur code projects/bojji" && python - <<'PY'
import pathlib
note = """#
# RELIEF CAP LEAKAGE GUARD. The $80,000 personal income tax relief cap is a
# GLOBAL cap on the TOTAL of all reliefs (in force from YA 2018), not a property
# of any single relief. IRAS repeats it as a warning on most individual relief
# pages -- it appears on 6 of the 8 relief pages fetched for this corpus,
# including this SOP's own source. It is deliberately NOT restated here: it
# belongs to SOP-REL-005, which is HELD OUT (sop_design.md S5).
#
# This suppression is what makes the partial-answer holdout real. The cap is the
# one relief fact that cannot be derived from any single relief's rules, because
# it is a property of the sum. If any indexed SOP restated it, the agent could
# answer the cap question from the index and the holdout would collapse into an
# ordinary answerable case. See the matching `do_not` entry below.
"""
for name, anchor in [
    ("SOP-REL-002", "# Class: tax_reliefs (auto_answerable). Second of four indexed relief SOPs.\n"),
    ("SOP-REL-004", "# COMPUTATION BOUNDARY: this SOP contains the ordering rule (QCR first, WMCR takes\n"),
]:
    p = pathlib.Path(f"data/sop_specs/{name}.yaml"); s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if "RELIEF CAP LEAKAGE GUARD" in s: print(f"{name}: already present"); continue
    s = s.replace(anchor, anchor + note, 1)
    p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8"); print(f"{name}: guard note added")

# REL-001 has the rationale inline already; REL-003's note understates the scope.
p = pathlib.Path("data/sop_specs/SOP-REL-003.yaml"); s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
old = """# NOTE: the source pages for both CPF and SRS relief mention the $80,000 personal
# relief cap in passing. That fact is deliberately NOT restated here — it belongs
# to SOP-REL-005, which is held out (sop_design.md S5). Repeating it would defeat
# the partial-answer holdout, since the agent could answer the cap question from
# an indexed SOP. Correct behaviour is to state eligibility and escalate the cap."""
new = """# RELIEF CAP LEAKAGE GUARD. The $80,000 personal income tax relief cap is a
# GLOBAL cap on the TOTAL of all reliefs (in force from YA 2018), not a property
# of CPF or SRS relief. IRAS repeats it as a warning on most individual relief
# pages -- it appears on 6 of the 8 relief pages fetched for this corpus, and the
# CPF and SRS pages are among the most emphatic because contributions there are
# irreversible. It is deliberately NOT restated here: it belongs to SOP-REL-005,
# which is HELD OUT (sop_design.md S5).
#
# This suppression is what makes the partial-answer holdout real. The cap is the
# one relief fact that cannot be derived from any single relief's rules, because
# it is a property of the sum. If any indexed SOP restated it, the agent could
# answer the cap question from the index and the holdout would collapse into an
# ordinary answerable case."""
assert old in s
p.write_text(s.replace(old, new, 1), encoding="utf-8"); print("SOP-REL-003: note corrected")
PY
